title: World-Forge RPG Profile
description: Interface contract between the World-Forge generation pipeline (producer) and the SillyTavern RPG engine (consumer). World-Forge writes RPG stat data; the RPG engine reads it to seed authoritative game state (active.json). A document is one of three kinds: a character profile (embedded in a card under data.extensions.world_forge_rpg), a standalone user profile, or a bestiary library of monsters. Numbers here are STARTING values only — once a game begins the engine owns mutation; this schema never carries live/per-turn state.

kind.description: Document discriminator. 'character_rpg_profile' is embedded in a card's data.extensions.world_forge_rpg; the others are standalone files.

schema_version.description: Semver of THIS schema the document was authored against. The engine validates major-version compatibility on import and refuses mismatches rather than guessing.

tierName.description: Severity bucket for an attack outcome. The small parser LLM emits one of these; the engine maps it to dice. This is the ONLY damage vocabulary that crosses the LLM boundary — raw numbers never do.

diceFormula.description: A droll-style dice expression (e.g. '2d6', '1d8+2') or a bare integer (e.g. '5'). Resolved server-side at apply time.

damageTierTable.description: Per-entity mapping of tier -> dice. This is how a tier-5 monster's 'heavy' hits harder than a tier-1's: each entity calibrates its own table. When absent, the engine falls back to its global rules.json table.

abilityScores.description: Optional D&D-style ability modifiers (already as modifiers, not raw 3-18 scores), matching the dnd-starter-kit convention.

item.description: A piece of equipment. Carried for reference and loot; the engine does NOT re-derive combat stats from items at runtime (see statBlock.combat — World-Forge emits resolved values). 'combat_mods' documents this item's contribution so a future /equip endpoint can recompute on loot/swap.

slot.description: Where the item is worn/wielded. 'none' for consumables/misc.

combat_mods.description: This item's contribution to the resolved combat profile. Additive bonuses; attack items may set a default attack tier.

combatProfile.description: The RESOLVED combat numbers the engine seeds directly into active.json. World-Forge computes these from base stats + equipment so the engine stays a pure calculator. armor_dr is flat damage reduction subtracted from each physical hit (the 'thick armor' model); ac is the avoidance value (harder to hit).

armor_dr.description: Flat damage reduction per physical hit.

conditions.description: Comma-free status label or 'none'. Starting condition only.

default_attack_tier.description: Tier this entity deals by default when the narration is vague about severity.

tier_shift.description: Optional resistance/weakness model that stays server-deterministic: per attack_type, shift the incoming tier by N steps (negative = resistant, positive = vulnerable). Example: {"slashing": -1} means heavy plate downgrades incoming slashes by one tier. Engine clamps within the tier list.

statBlock.description: The full RPG stat object for a single entity (character, user, or monster). 'combat' is mandatory (what the engine seeds); the rest is descriptive/progression context World-Forge may carry for richer play.

id.description: Stable snake_case identifier used as the entity key in active.json and as the attacker/target id the parser LLM emits.

progression.description: Optional hook for World-Forge's existing arc/progression model (XP, milestones). The engine ignores unknown progression fields.

characterProfile.description: Embedded in a V3 card at data.extensions.world_forge_rpg. The character's id should be stable across the world; display_name typically mirrors the card's data.name.

world_id.description: Optional link back to the World-Forge world this character belongs to, so the engine can pair the right bestiary/user files.

userProfile.description: Standalone file for the player persona (personas lack a rich card extensions field, so the user's RPG stats live here). The engine seeds this as the 'player' entity.

stats.description: The player's stat block. By convention stats.id is 'player' so it matches the engine's default entity key.

bestiary.description: Read-only monster library for a world. The engine never mutates this; on spawn it COPIES a monster's stat block into active.json as a combat instance, mutates the copy per turn, and discards it when the monster is vanquished — the library stays intact.

global_damage_tiers.description: Optional bestiary-wide fallback tier table for monsters that don't define their own.

monster.description: A monster template. 'tier' (1-5) drives encounter scaling; 'boss' marks named/elite foes. Multiple instances of the same template spawn with distinct instance ids appended by the engine (e.g. goblin_raider#2).

loot_table.description: Optional items that may drop on defeat, for a future loot/equip flow.
